entries.context: At an October 22, 2024 campaign rally, Trump advocated no tax on tips. Public Law 119-21 subsequently established a temporary federal income-tax deduction for qualifying tips (tax years 2025–2028), subject to eligibility conditions and a $25,000 annual limit. This is not an exemption from all taxes on tip income; applicable payroll taxes remain. The record documents a related enacted policy, not a determination of full fulfillment or voter intent.

At an October 22, 2024 campaign rally, Trump advocated no tax on overtime. Public Law 119-21 later established a temporary federal income-tax deduction for qualifying overtime premium compensation (tax years 2025–2028), with annual limits of $12,500 ($25,000 for joint filers) and income-based phaseouts. The deduction does not eliminate all taxes on all overtime earnings. The record notes a related policy action without treating the campaign slogan as fully enacted.

entries.commitment: Make interest on loans for domestically manufactured automobiles tax-deductible
entries.context: At an October 22, 2024 campaign rally, Trump proposed deductibility of auto-loan interest for qualifying U.S.-built cars. Public Law 119-21 later introduced a deduction of up to $10,000 per year for eligible interest on loans for new, U.S.-assembled personal vehicles, generally for tax years 2025–2028 and subject to eligibility and income limits. Used vehicles and leases do not qualify. This record does not imply that every auto loan qualifies.

entries.commitment: Eliminate federal income taxes on Social Security benefits
entries.context: At an October 22, 2024 campaign rally Trump advocated no tax on Social Security benefits. Public Law 119-21, enacted July 4, 2025, instead created a temporary additional deduction of up to $6,000 per eligible person aged 65 or older for tax years 2025–2028 (up to $12,000 for eligible married couples filing jointly), subject to income phaseouts and other requirements. This deduction is not specific to Social Security recipients and does not repeal federal taxation of Social Security benefits; some benefits remain taxable depending on income. The law therefore constitutes related tax relief, not enactment of the stated exemption. IRS guidance: https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/working-families-tax-cuts-tax-deductions-for-working-americans-and-seniors and https://www.irs.gov/faqs/social-security-income
entries.action_date_description: Public Law 119-21 enacted a temporary enhanced deduction for qualifying seniors, not a Social Security tax exemption

entries.election_cycle: 2020 Georgia U.S. Senate regular election (January 2021 runoff)
entries.commitment: Place personal stock portfolio in a blind trust and champion legislation requiring blind trusts for members of Congress
entries.context: In an October 20, 2020 candidate Q&A, Ossoff pledged to put his stock portfolio into a blind trust on taking office and advocate legislation requiring blind trusts for members of Congress. The Congressional Record confirms he was sworn in January 20, 2021 (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CREC-2021-01-20/pdf/CREC-2021-01-20-dailydigest.pdf). His official Senate office announced on June 9, 2021 that the transfer had been completed (https://www.ossoff.senate.gov/press-releases/senator-ossoff-leads-on-ethics-fulfills-campaign-promise-to-move-stocks-into-blind-trust/). The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported on June 9 that he notified the Senate during the preceding week of establishing a qualified blind trust (https://www.ajc.com/politics/sen-jon-ossoff-fulfills-campaign-promise-by-putting-assets-in-blind-trust/SUSDSU7E6JE63CGIAROQ4DO2ZU/). This supports eventual trust establishment, but does not establish completion on inauguration day; timing of the original day-one pledge is not verified. Ossoff and Sen. Mark Kelly later introduced stock-trading legislation, which is distinct from enactment of a binding prohibition. An office announcement is not an independent trust instrument; do not infer broader congressional compliance or law passage.
entries.action_date_description: Senate office announced stock portfolio moved into blind trust; related legislation introduced January 12, 2022

entries.commitment: Further reduce prescription drug costs through most-favored-nation pricing
entries.context: At a September 25, 2020 reelection campaign rally in Newport News, Trump said his administration was instituting a 'favored nations' approach and promised lower prescription drug costs. This was a campaign statement by an incumbent who lost the 2020 election, not evidence of savings. Executive Order 13948 was issued September 13, before this campaign statement. CMS published the Most Favored Nation Medicare Part B model interim final rule November 27, 2020. A nationwide preliminary injunction on December 28 prevented its planned January 1, 2021 implementation. CMS later rescinded the rule, effective February 28, 2022. The model was never implemented as planned, and no savings from this model are established. The proposal concerned selected Medicare Part B drugs, not all prescription medicines. Campaign transcript: https://rollcall.com/factbase/trump/transcript/donald-trump-speech-campaign-rally-newport-news-virginia-september-25-2020 ; official implementation and rescission record: https://www.cms.gov/priorities/innovation/innovation-models/most-favored-nation-model ; rescission rule: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2021/12/29/2021-28225/most-favored-nation-mfn-model .
entries.action_date_description: CMS interim final rule published; subsequently enjoined before implementation and rescinded

entries.commitment: I will rejoin the Paris Climate Accord
entries.context: In a July 11, 2019 campaign foreign-policy address (archived as prepared for delivery), Biden pledged to rejoin the Paris Climate Accord. Biden won the 2020 presidential election (306 electoral votes). On January 20, 2021, he signed the United States' instrument of acceptance; the Department of State confirmed that the United States became a party again on February 19, 2021. Rejoining through the President's foreign-affairs authority is a distinct action from delivering emissions reductions or achieving broader climate goals. Later development: the United States notified the UN depositary of withdrawal on January 27, 2025, and that withdrawal became effective January 27, 2026, as recorded by the UNFCCC (https://unfccc.int/node/61231) and the UN depositary (https://treaties.un.org/doc/Publication/CN/2025/CN.71.2025-Eng.pdf). This subsequent change in party status does not negate the documented 2021 rejoining and does not establish any particular emissions outcome. The source is an as-prepared speech, not independently verified verbatim delivery.
entries.action_date_description: United States formally rejoined Paris Agreement following Jan. 20 presidential acceptance

entries.commitment: I will end the Muslim ban
entries.context: In a July 11, 2019 campaign foreign-policy address (archived as prepared for delivery), Biden pledged to end what he called the Muslim ban. Biden won the 2020 presidential election (306 electoral votes). Presidential Proclamation 10141, issued January 20, 2021, revoked specified earlier entry-restriction proclamations and directed further agency reviews. The President could revoke predecessor presidential proclamations within applicable law; the record does not establish that every visa application was granted or that all immigration restrictions ended. The source is an as-prepared speech, not independently verified verbatim delivery.
entries.action_date_description: Presidential Proclamation 10141 revoked specified entry restrictions

entries.commitment: I will announce our withdrawal from the Trans-Pacific Partnership
entries.context: In his October 22, 2016 Gettysburg campaign address, Trump pledged that on the first day of his administration he would announce U.S. withdrawal from the Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP). The American Presidency Project archives the dated speech (https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/remarks-proposals-for-the-first-100-days-office-the-eisenhower-complex-gettysburg); the contemporaneous campaign contract is preserved at https://p2016.org/trump/trump102216sp.html . On January 23, 2017, three days after inauguration, President Trump signed a memorandum directing the U.S. Trade Representative to withdraw the United States as a signatory and permanently withdraw from TPP negotiations (Federal Register, 82 FR 8497, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2017-01-25/pdf/2017-01845.pdf). This documents withdrawal action, but not performance of the promised first-day timing. The TPP was not ratified by the United States and was not an operative U.S. trade law being repealed. No employment, wage, or trade-balance outcome is established by the memorandum alone.
entries.action_date_description: Presidential memorandum directing withdrawal from TPP signatory status and negotiations; signed three days after inauguration

entries.commitment: Institute a five-year lobbying ban for former executive branch officials
entries.context: At an October 18, 2016 campaign rally in Colorado Springs, Trump promised a five-year ban on executive-branch officials lobbying government after leaving office. On January 28, 2017, he signed Executive Order 13770, requiring covered executive-branch appointees to agree not to lobby their former agency for five years after service. This is narrower than a blanket ban on lobbying all of government and did not enact his separate call for a five-year congressional lobbying ban. The order provided waiver mechanisms. On January 19, 2021, Executive Order 13983 revoked EO 13770, as documented by the Congressional Research Service. The order's issuance establishes a related executive action, not universal enforcement, congressional enactment, or lasting reform. Original campaign remarks are archived as delivered by the American Presidency Project; source on revocation: https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/R/PDF/R44974/R44974.4.pdf .
entries.action_date_description: Executive Order 13770 signed, restricting covered appointees' lobbying of former agencies for five years; later revoked January 19, 2021

entries.commitment: Pass the Military Parental Leave Modernization Act to provide at least 12 weeks of paid parental leave to service members regardless of gender or sexual orientation
entries.context: In a first-person August 1, 2016 public statement during her Senate campaign, then-Representative Tammy Duckworth called for passage of the Military Parental Leave Modernization Act (H.R. 4796), which she had already introduced in March 2016. Her original bill did not become law. A later, distinct bipartisan FY2022 National Defense Authorization Act, signed December 27, 2021, expanded eligible military parental leave to 12 weeks for birth, adoption, or long-term foster placement. The later provision is related policy progress, not passage of her original bill or evidence that Duckworth alone caused its enactment. Congressional Research Service comparison: https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IN/PDF/IN11802/IN11802.3.pdf
entries.action_date_description: FY2022 National Defense Authorization Act signed into law with a related, distinct expansion of military parental leave

entries.commitment: Redeploy combat brigades from Iraq within 16 months, retaining limited residual forces
entries.context: A July 19, 2008 campaign release quoted senior national security adviser Susan Rice confirming Obama's support for a 16-month redeployment timetable. Obama's March 19 Fayetteville speech also described a 16-month plan with residual forces for diplomatic protection and counterterrorism (https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/obama-we-must-end-the-iraq-war-address-our-national-security-priorities). Obama won 365 electoral votes to McCain's 173 (https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2008). As commander in chief he could direct deployments subject to statutory, funding and international constraints. On February 27, 2009 he announced a revised 18-month drawdown plan (https://obamawhitehouse.archives.gov/the-press-office/remarks-president-barack-obama-ndash-responsibly-ending-war-iraq). On August 31, 2010 he announced the end of the combat mission, with transitional forces remaining. This was later than the original 16-month timetable and did not mean all personnel had left. The announcement also identified an agreed end-2011 withdrawal deadline. Independent verification of final withdrawal and longer-term security outcomes remains outside this entry.
entries.action_date_description: President announced end of combat mission, with transitional forces remaining

entries.commitment: I propose a plan to build 45 new nuclear plants before the year 2030
entries.context: CNN's August 6, 2008 transcript preserves McCain's own remarks proposing 45 new nuclear plants and projecting employment gains. McCain lost the presidential election, receiving 173 electoral votes to Obama's 365 (https://www.archives.gov/electoral-college/2008). A president could advocate energy legislation and direct lawful executive policy, but construction would depend on financing, licensing, utilities and other actors. No McCain presidential term existed against which to evaluate implementation. The target year 2030 is beyond this review date. No jobs outcome or failure determination is inferred.

date_field_notes.commitment_date: Date of the cited campaign statement (not necessarily the first time the commitment was made)
date_field_notes.action_date: Date of the related government action identified in the entry
date_field_notes.reviewed_on: Last editorial review date; not a government action date
